title: The local-to-global spectral sequence for sheaf Ext
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme (quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]) and let $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ be coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules [pqf-def-coherent]. There is a spectral sequence $E_2^{p,q}=H^p(X,\mathcal Ext^q_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G))\Rightarrow\operatorname{Ext}^{p+q}_X(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)$, with $E_2^{p,q}=0$ unless $p,q\geq0$, where $H^p(X,-)$ is the cohomology of [pqf-def-cohomology], $\mathcal Ext^q$ the sheaf Ext of [def-weil-pbc-sheaf-ext], and the abutment is the Ext of [def-sc-ext-sheaf]. In particular, if $d\geq0$ is an integer and $E_2^{p,q}=0$ for all $p+q>d$, then $\operatorname{Ext}^n_X(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)=0$ for every $n>d$.

source.place: Lemma lemma-Ext-0-regular (Tag 0FZ3), proof of (1), spectral sequence; Cohomology Section Tag 0BQP

proof.text: Work in the abelian categories of $\mathcal O_X$-modules and abelian groups, with $T=\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,-)$ and $U=\Gamma(X,-)$. Both functors are left exact additive [def-sp-left-exact-additive]; $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ is Grothendieck abelian by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] (the site of open subsets of $X$ is small) and abelian groups $=\Mod(\mathbf Z)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-grothendieck-abelian], so $(T,U)$ is a composable pair; the module category has enough injectives [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-modules-enough-injectives], and [lem-sc-ext-coherent-hom-injective-acyclic] supplies that $T$ sends injectives to $U$-acyclic objects. Therefore [thm-sp-grothendieck] gives a functorial first-quadrant spectral sequence $E_2^{p,q}=R^pU(R^qT(\mathcal G))$ converging to $R^{p+q}(U\circ T)(\mathcal G)$.

source.place: Lemma 0FZ3, proof of (1), construction of the local-to-global Ext spectral sequence

proof.text: For an injective resolution $\mathcal G\to\mathcal I^\bullet$, the complex $\mathcal I^\bullet$ is K-injective [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective], so by the definition of sheaf Ext [def-weil-pbc-sheaf-ext] $\mathcal Ext^q_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)=\mathcal H^q(\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\mathcal F[0],\mathcal I^\bullet))=\mathcal H^q(\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,\mathcal I^\bullet))=R^qT(\mathcal G)$, and by [pqf-def-cohomology] $R^pU(-)=H^p(X,-)$. By the injective-resolution computation of Ext [lem-weil-pbc-ext-via-injective-resolution] (using the corrected meaning of the Ext group), since $U\circ T=\Gamma(X,\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,-))=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,-)$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom], $R^{p+q}(U\circ T)(\mathcal G)=\operatorname{Ext}^{p+q}_X(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)$. Substitution gives the displayed $E_2$-page and abutment; first-quadrantness gives vanishing unless $p,q\geq0$.

source.place: Section 0BQP, sheaf Ext and global Ext identifications

proof.text: A first-quadrant spectral sequence induces a finite exhaustive filtration on each abutment group in a fixed total degree. If every $E_2^{p,q}$ with $p+q>d$ is zero, all later pages and the associated graded pieces in total degree $n>d$ are zero; the filtration therefore has zero abutment, so $\operatorname{Ext}^n_X(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)=0$ for every $n>d$.
